environment.tool: manual audit of the final tag source + live compiled binary; raw-socket client sending exact bytes, strict-token upstream peer logging verbatim request bytes and byte count

findings.description: The store copies response headers verbatim, so an upstream gzip body stored under |* arrives with Content-Encoding: gzip at a victim that sent no Accept-Encoding. Same on all three wildcard builds; 6baf167b never does it because it stores only exact keys. Cosmetic-to-breaking depending on the client.
findings.title: A wildcard entry carrying Content-Encoding: gzip is served to clients that never advertised gzip

limitations: All RCE in this corpus is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Control request first on the same config
Raw client bytes and raw upstream bytes captured in hex
Payload diffed against the control line

author_attested: analysis metadata reconstructed after the run
provenance.release_metadata: historical release.json omitted the tag field; tag resolved from the existing Git tag and verified against the submitted source
verified: release tag resolves to the submitted source
source SHA-256 and report and evidence hashes

scope: Consumer-parity: whether each build s RCE is still an executing request when the upstream is stock software (nginx + FastCGI, node 22 / llhttp, python http.server) instead of a hand-written peer. Execution is always on the upstream host; the proxy never executes.
